hlido_opinion.headline: Generates genuinely editable PowerPoint — native shapes and animations, not flat slide images — which is the one feature that separates useful deck generators from demos.
hlido_opinion.body: PPT Master's differentiator is specific and well-chosen: it produces real, natively editable .pptx files with native shapes and animations, optionally following your own template, rather than exporting slide images you can't touch. That distinction is the whole game in this category — a generator that hands you an un-editable deck has offloaded the easy 80% and kept you from doing the 20% that matters, and the project says so plainly ('a natively editable deck exists precisely so you can keep working on it'). Speaker notes voiced as audio narration is a reasonable adjacent feature, and multi-model support (Claude, OpenAI, Gemini) is sensible. One claim to read with care is the 'as low as 7% of official rates' model pricing — that is an economics claim about a model-access arrangement, not about output quality, and a buyer should understand exactly what they are routing through before relying on it. This is a public-surface and repository read, so the editability and quality claims reflect the project's own framing rather than a generated-deck inspection in this review.

tier_rationale: STEADY (80) because the product targets the one feature that actually matters in deck generation — true .pptx editability with native shapes and templates — and backs it with sensible adjacent features (audio narration, multi-model, MIT licence). Not higher because the editability and quality claims were read on the public surface rather than verified on generated output, and the low-cost model-access framing needs buyer scrutiny.
what_it_does_well: Produces natively editable .pptx with real shapes and animations, not slide images
Can follow the user's own .pptx template rather than imposing a fixed style
Speaker notes voiced as audio narration out of the box
what_it_fails_at: Editability and quality-ceiling claims were read, not verified on generated decks here
The 'as low as 7% of official rates' model-pricing framing needs buyer scrutiny
Output still needs human polish — positioned as taking tedious work off your plate, not finishing it
Quality is said to vary by model, with a stated ceiling on non-preferred models
best_for: Users who need editable decks they can keep refining, not static exports
Teams with an existing .pptx template they must conform to
Document-to-deck workflows where native PowerPoint fidelity matters
not_recommended_for: Users who want a finished, no-edit deck with zero human polish
Buyers uncomfortable routing model access through a discounted arrangement
Anyone needing a hosted, non-technical, click-only product (this is a repo/tool)

compared_to.verdict_diff: Genspark is a broad agentic suite that includes slide generation among many outputs; PPT Master is specialised in editable .pptx fidelity. Choose PPT Master when native PowerPoint editability is the requirement, Genspark for breadth.

evidence_urls.claim: Generates a real, editable PowerPoint from any document with native shapes and animations
Can follow your own .pptx template rather than producing slide images
Speaker notes voiced as audio narration; multi-model support (Claude, OpenAI, Gemini)

agent_relevance.agent_integration_path: PPT Master runs as a document-to-deck pipeline that can be invoked from a command line, so an agent workflow could drive it to produce .pptx artifacts. No documented API or MCP server for other agents to call directly.
